title: ALTO: African and Levantine Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence Corpus
abstract: arXiv:2611.06706v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Tech-facilitated gender based violence (TFGBV) is a pervasive online harm affecting women and gender minority groups through its many direct and covert forms. Current models and annotated datasets for gendered harm detection are dominated by data from, and models trained in, Global North languages. In collaboration with civil society organizations (CSOs) from Jordan, Francophone West Africa, and Kenya, we developed a community-led approach to crowdsource culturally and linguistically relevant instances of TFGBV in Levantine Arabic, African French, and Swahili. We annotated the crowdsourced data using active learning to develop a small but performant dataset (N=3022) called ALTO to improve TFGBV detection in the three languages. Through benchmarking and fine-tuning experiments, we show that existing harmful content detection models show poor TFGBV recall within ALTO and improve with fine-tuning. translated_title: ALTO：非洲与黎凡特地区技术助长的基于性别的暴力语料库
translated_abstract: 技术助长的基于性别的暴力（TFGBV）是一种普遍存在的网络危害，通过多种直接和隐蔽的形式影响女性和性别少数群体。当前用于性别伤害检测的模型和标注数据集主要被来自全球北方语言的数据以及用这些语言训练的模型所主导。我们与来自约旦、法语西非和肯尼亚的民间社会组织（CSOs）合作，开发了一种社区主导的方法，通过众包方式收集黎凡特阿拉伯语、非洲法语和斯瓦希里语中符合当地文化和语言特点的TFGBV实例。我们使用主动学习对众包数据进行标注，构建了一个规模虽小但性能出色的数据集（N=3022），命名为ALTO，用于改进这三种语言的TFGBV检测。通过基准测试和微调实验，我们表明现有的有害内容检测模型在ALTO数据集上的TFGBV召回率较低，而经过微调后性能有所提升。我们发现模型往往无法识别隐蔽的……
tldr: 该论文通过与约旦、西非和肯尼亚的民间社会组织合作，以社区主导的众包方式构建了首个涵盖黎凡特阿拉伯语、非洲法语和斯瓦希里语的技术助长性别暴力标注语料库ALTO，填补了现有性别伤害检测研究长期偏向全球北方语言的空白。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ALTO, a community-led crowdsourced corpus (N=3022) for tech-facilitated gender-based violence detection in Levantine Arabic, African French, and Swahili, addressing the Global North language bias in existing gendered harm detection datasets and showing that fine-tuning improves model recall on covert TFGBV cases.
